newsitem.title: GREECE: Banks, industrials push Greek shares above 1,600pts.
newsitem.headline: Banks, industrials push Greek shares above 1,600pts.

text.p: Greek shares blew through the 1,600 barrier in early Tuesday trade as banks and industrials staged a strong performance on the back of yet another round of lending and savings rate cuts.

The Athens general index opened with a jolt to 1,606.75 from Friday's close of 1,595.54. It stood at 1,618.83, up 23.29 points or 1.46 percent, after 25 minutes of trading, having set a new year high of 1,624.63 earlier.
Banks and industrials were up 1.40 and 1.85 percent, respectively, with other sectors mixed.
The widespread mood of optimism was mainly the product of drastic cuts in lending and savings rates announced by Alpha Credit Bank on Monday.

"A cut in interest rates was on the cards following the easing of inflation and Alpha Credit typically assumes the leading role in rate changes. However, the magnitude of the rate cuts was not anticipated," said Petros Parisi, broker at Nuntius Securities.
A correction in prices was in the back of brokers' minds but it was seen as an opportunity for additional equity purchases.

"Technically speaking, a correction will come about as gains need be realised. The market has sufficient momentum to keep on appreciating on a milder tone towards its medium-term targets," said Parisis.

"In the event of a mild correction, we suggest purchases ... given the market's medium-term target of 1,675 points. Stocks should not be chased upwards," said Kondor, the investment services company (EPEY), in its weekly strategy report.
Buyers were shifting their interest towards middle caps, though banks and large cap industrial stocks were still the hottest picks, brokers said.
"More buy orders are placed for middle cap stocks in food, construction and mettalurgy, but there appears no sign of fatigue in banks and large industrials," Parisis said.
Turnover amounted to 5.2 billion drachmas on 1.27 million shares traded. Advancers led decliners 109 to 66 with 34 stocks unchanged on 209 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted unchanged at 1,099-1,129. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 80 drachmas at 6,630.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $84.87-$86.57. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 3,493-3,615 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $21.25-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
